title: Versions and staleness against the logbook
summary: Blueprint.read lists (where, order, page; answers { items, next }) through the model, store, server, sdk, cli and docs. Compare.release works the next version out from the model diff (minor, major, patch); architect version --next and architect impact (next, stale <ops> in <envs>) read the last release and main's verdicts from the logbook; generated/model/changes.json is written; Releases.record PUTs the model and POSTs the release for L2.05.
proves: Against the real logbook and a real OIDC issuer: adding allowance.list gives next 1.1.0 and stale none; a budget edit is a patch and stales exactly allowance.spend in staging and production; a changed payload is a major; a pull request's verdict never counts. On a real world, a list's where, order, page and cursor work, roles are enforced, and allowance.list passes all nine evals. Gate 1's checks and acme and the starter's local prove stay green.
